articles.title: UK-backed AI chip startup Fractile hits $7 billion valuation in funding round
articles.snippet: UK-backed AI chip startup Fractile hits $7 billion valuation in funding round The Mighty 790 KFGO
articles.text:
By Sam Tabahriti
LONDON, Nov 11 (Reuters) – AI chip startup Fractile was valued at $7 billion in its latest fundraising round, which included backing from the British government, a person involved ​in the deal said on Wednesday, making it one ‌of Britain’s most valuable technology startups.
The London- and Bristol-based company is developing chips designed to improve AI inference, the process through which AI models generate responses. Fractile says its technology can deliver faster performance while cutting energy use ‌and ​costs.
The company raised $720 million in a Series ⁠C funding round led ⁠by Thrive Capital, Founders Fund, Lightspeed and Redpoint, it told Reuters.
Other investors included Google’s venture arm CapitalG, BlackRock, DST Global, Elad Gil, Balderton, SV Angel, Britain’s Sovereign AI fund and the ​British Business Bank.
BRITAIN’S AI AMBITIONS
The investment marks a major vote of confidence in Britain’s efforts to build domestic AI infrastructure, rather ⁠than solely relying on overseas suppliers ⁠for the computing power that underpins the technology.
It also ​highlights growing investor interest in companies developing the hardware behind AI, ​a market dominated by Nvidia and a handful of Asian ‌semiconductor manufacturers.
Britain has made becoming an AI superpower a key part of its economic strategy, seeking to build on strengths in AI research and chip design while retaining more of the jobs, ⁠investment and economic value generated by the technology.
“For too long, Britain has produced some of the world’s best scientific ideas, only to see too ⁠much of the ‌technology, industry and wealth they create built elsewhere,” ⁠AI Minister Kanishka Narayan said in a statement ​on the ‌funding round.
“We are determined to change that.”
Britain is ​home to ⁠chip designer Arm, whose technology is used in billions of devices worldwide, but its semiconductor manufacturing industry remains small compared with those in the US and Asia.
Fractile plans to launch its first commercial chip next year.
($1 = 0.7492 pounds)
(Reporting by Sam Tabahriti. Editing by Adam Jourdan ​and Mark Potter)

UK-Backed AI Chip Startup Fractile Reaches $7B Valuation in $720M Series C
By James Dargan · 13 November 2026 · 1 min read
Fractile, a London- and Bristol-based AI chip startup, has been valued at $7 billion after securing $720 million in a Series C round that included backing from the British government, making it one of the UK’s most valuable technology startups.
The round was led by Thrive Capital, Founders Fund, Lightspeed and Redpoint, with participation from Google’s venture arm CapitalG, BlackRock, DST Global, Elad Gil, Balderton, SV Angel, Britain’s Sovereign AI fund and the British Business Bank.
Fractile is developing chips designed to improve AI inference, the process by which AI models generate responses, and says its technology delivers faster performance while reducing energy use and costs. The company plans to release its first commercial chip next year.
The deal signals confidence in Britain’s push to build domestic AI infrastructure rather than relying solely on overseas computing power, and reflects growing investor interest in AI hardware, a market dominated by Nvidia and a small group of Asian manufacturers.
AI Minister Kanishka Narayan said Britain has too often produced world-leading scientific ideas only to see the resulting technology, industry and wealth built elsewhere, and that the government is determined to change that. While the UK is home to chip designer Arm, its semiconductor manufacturing industry remains small compared with the US and Asia.

News / Technology
Nvidia Rival Fractile Hits $7B Valuation With $720M AI Chip Funding
British AI chip startup Fractile raises $720M at a $7B valuation, backed by Google, BlackRock and the UK government ahead of its 2027 chip launch.
Emir Abyazov 2 min read
12 November 2026, 01:14 PM Prefer us on Google
Key takeaways
Fractile raises $720 million at $7 billion valuation
Google and UK government back Nvidia challenger
First commercial AI chips expected in 2027
British AI chip startup Fractile has raised $720 million at a $7 billion valuation, attracting backing from Google-linked investors, BlackRock and the UK government as competition intensifies to develop alternatives to Nvidia's artificial intelligence processors.
The November 11 Series C round was co-led by Thrive Capital, Founders Fund, Lightspeed and Redpoint. Alphabet's CapitalG, DST Global, Balderton and several other investors also participated.
The UK government's announcement confirmed investments from its Sovereign AI fund and the British Business Bank, describing the financing as part of Britain's strategy to develop domestic semiconductor capabilities.
Fractile's $720M Funding Targets Nvidia's AI Chip Dominance
Founded in 2022 by Walter Goodwin, Fractile is developing processors specifically designed for AI inference, the process of generating responses after a model has been trained.
Unlike conventional AI accelerators, Fractile's architecture places dynamic random-access memory directly above processing components, seeking to reduce the delays caused by moving data between memory and computing units.
The company argues that memory bandwidth increasingly limits AI performance, particularly as reasoning models and autonomous agents generate longer outputs.
Its technology could eventually challenge Nvidia's dominant position in AI inference, although commercial performance remains unproven.
The financing arrives as Google expands its exposure to alternative AI chip developers, including a recently disclosed $548 million Qualcomm stake.
Other companies are pursuing similar opportunities through custom AI accelerators , as cloud providers seek more specialized computing hardware.
Google and UK Government Back Fractile's Expansion
Fractile's investors include major technology-focused funds alongside British public institutions, reflecting growing demand for alternatives to foreign semiconductor suppliers.
The British government said the investment would help the company expand its engineering operations across London and Bristol while strengthening domestic AI infrastructure.
The round also comes amid Nvidia's continued investment in AI chip research , where rapid innovation remains essential to protecting its competitive advantage.
However, Fractile faces significant execution challenges.
The company expects to introduce its first commercial chip in 2027, meaning its current valuation largely reflects investor expectations rather than established product revenue.
Can Fractile Challenge Nvidia in AI Inference?
Fractile is entering a competitive market that includes established semiconductor companies and emerging developers such as Groq and Etched.
Nvidia has already pursued inference technology investments to strengthen its position as AI workloads expand beyond model training.
Fractile must demonstrate that its architecture delivers meaningful improvements in speed, energy consumption and cost under real-world conditions.

articles.text:
Surgery Partners: HealthSpan Partners Raises Merger Offer To $25 Per Share In Deal Valued At Up To $6 Billion
By Amit Chowdhry
Yesterday at 3:32 PM
Surgery Partners: HealthSpan Partners Raises Merger Offer To $25 Per Share In Deal Valued At Up To $6 Billion
Surgery Partners and HealthSpan Partners have amended their merger agreement to increase the cash consideration for Surgery Partners shareholders to $25 per share, with the total enterprise value potentially reaching approximately $6 billion. The revised agreement follows an unsolicited competing acquisition proposal and includes additional payments for certain shareholders if the transaction closes after March 1, 2027.
HealthSpan Partners is affiliated with Bon Secours Mercy Health and is pursuing the acquisition of Surgery Partners, an operator of outpatient surgical facilities across the United States.
The amendment represents an increase in the merger consideration and introduces a mechanism to compensate eligible shareholders for certain closing delays.
Under the amended agreement, shareholders other than affiliates of Bain Capital will receive $25 per share in cash if the transaction closes before March 1, 2027.
If the required shareholder approval has been obtained but the transaction remains incomplete after that date, eligible shareholders will receive additional monthly payments.
These payments will accrue at a rate equivalent to 10% annually on the $25-per-share merger consideration.
If the transaction closes on its October 23, 2027 outside date and the applicable conditions are satisfied, those payments could total up to $1.61 per share.
That would increase the maximum consideration for eligible shareholders to $26.61 per share.
The revised merger agreement follows an unsolicited, nonbinding competing proposal received on November 3, 2026, and updated on November 8.
The competing bidder offered $28 per share in cash to acquire all outstanding Surgery Partners shares.
Although the competing proposal offered a higher stated price, Surgery Partners’ independent special committee considered additional factors involving transaction certainty and closing timing.
The committee evaluated the likelihood that the competing transaction would receive regulatory approvals and the potential consequences of a longer completion process.
It also considered the contractual protections available under each proposal.
Following consultation with legal and financial advisors, the special committee unanimously determined that the competing offer did not constitute a superior proposal under the existing merger agreement.
The committee recommended that Surgery Partners proceed with the amended HealthSpan transaction.
The company’s Board of Directors approved the revised agreement and reaffirmed its recommendation that shareholders vote in favor of the merger.
Bain Capital, which owns approximately 39% of Surgery Partners’ outstanding shares, has agreed to support the transaction.
Rather than receiving cash consideration, Bain Capital affiliates will exchange their Surgery Partners shares for ownership interests in the acquiring entity.
The arrangement will allow Bain Capital to remain a significant investor alongside HealthSpan Partners after closing.
Surgery Partners operates more than 200 locations across 30 states.
Its facilities include ambulatory surgery centers, surgical hospitals, multispecialty physician practices, and urgent care locations.

SoftBank Bets approximately $5.4 Billion on Swiss Robotics as Foreign Capital Influx Deepens
Add preferred source
Japan's SoftBank Group is pouring large sums into Switzerland's robotics industry, agreeing to acquire ABB's robotics division for $5.4 billion and investing $200 million in Gravis Robotics, a construction-robotics startup spun out of ETH Zurich. Foreign investors account for 88% of capital in deep-tech funding rounds of $100 million or more, and 43% of Swiss scale-ups are university or research-institute spin-offs. However, the share of Swiss investors in later-stage rounds has fallen from 27% to 13%, with limited mass-production experience and the flight of domestic capital cited as challenges at the growth stage.
Key Elements
SoftBank Group ABB Gravis Robotics ETH Zurich Deep Tech Nation Switzerland Switzerland Global Enterprise (S-GE) Neura Robotics Swissmem Swisscom Ventures EPFL
Japan's SoftBank Group is injecting large sums into Switzerland's robotics industry in quick succession. After agreeing to acquire the robotics division of Swiss automation company ABB for $5.4 billion (~7.2 trillion won), SoftBank in August invested $200 million (~270 billion won) in Gravis Robotics, a construction-robotics startup spun out of ETH Zurich. Gravis said the round was the largest Series A investment ever in the construction-robotics sector.
SoftBank's string of bets encapsulates the recent surge of foreign capital into Swiss deep-tech companies. According to the "Swiss Scale-up Report 2026" published this year by Deep Tech Nation Switzerland, foreign investors accounted for 88% of the capital in deep-tech funding rounds that raised $100 million or more. In effect, Swiss companies are raising their growth capital from abroad.
Speaking at a robotics and automation event hosted by Switzerland Global Enterprise (S-GE) in Zurich, Switzerland, on the 11th (local time), investment and industry officials agreed that foreign capital looks at the depth of research accumulated before a company's founding rather than its short history. They explained that technology and intellectual property (IP) built up over years in university labs, combined with research talent from around the world, heighten investment appeal.
Alexandre Meldem, head of international communications at Deep Tech Nation Switzerland, said, "Even if a company was only recently founded, there may be 10 years of science behind it," adding, "Switzerland is a relatively stable country with a predictable policy environment, which is an advantage because it allows investors to look 10 years ahead."
Indeed, research institutions are the key starting point for deep-tech companies in Switzerland. Of 265 Swiss scale-ups, 115—or 43%—are spin-offs from universities or research institutes. Forty-two came from ETH and 41 from EPFL. Some foreign robotics companies have even set up bases in Zurich directly to tap the research ecosystem. German robotics company Neura Robotics is developing core hardware technology for humanoid robots in Zurich.
Urs Laupi, chief strategy officer (CSO) of Neura Robotics, cited cooperation with ETH, physical AI research talent, and the capital environment as reasons for choosing Zurich as its base. "Switzerland has a solid knowledge base in the field of physical AI," he said, stressing that "we can combine world-class Swiss research capabilities with Germany's industrialization capabilities."

articles.text:
Mubadala Capital: LSV Advisors $5 Billion Secondaries Platform To Receive Strategic Minority Investment
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 9:38 AM
Mubadala Capital: LSV Advisors $5 Billion Secondaries Platform To Receive Strategic Minority Investment
Mubadala Capital, the alternative asset management subsidiary of Mubadala Investment Company, has entered into a definitive agreement to acquire a minority ownership stake in LSV Advisors, a New York-based investment manager specializing in GP-led secondary transactions. The partnership will expand Mubadala Capital’s alternative investment capabilities while supporting the continued growth of LSV, which manages approximately $5 billion in assets and commitments.
Founded in 2005, LSV has established a specialized investment strategy focused on general partner-led continuation vehicles, particularly single-asset transactions involving middle-market companies.
The firm has completed more than 75 transactions since executing one of the industry’s earliest GP-led investments in 2011.
Continuation vehicles have become an increasingly important segment of the private equity secondary market, providing investment managers with an alternative to selling portfolio companies through traditional exit transactions.
These structures allow general partners to transfer investments from an existing fund into a new investment vehicle, often providing existing limited partners with an opportunity to receive liquidity or maintain exposure to the underlying business.
For fund managers, continuation vehicles can create additional time to execute growth strategies at portfolio companies while introducing new capital partners.
LSV focuses on identifying established, cash-generative businesses and structuring investments that emphasize governance, risk management, and alignment among stakeholders.
The company’s approach combines investment due diligence with transaction structures designed to address the interests of general partners, existing investors, and new capital providers.
The investment will add dedicated GP-led secondaries expertise to Mubadala Capital’s expanding portfolio of strategic partnerships.
Mubadala Capital currently maintains investment relationships across private wealth, insurance, credit, and real estate.
The LSV partnership will complement those activities by providing exposure to a specialized segment of the private equity market.
Mubadala Capital manages, advises, and administers more than $755 billion in assets through its core alternative investment businesses and strategic partnerships.
Its core alternatives operations manage and invest more than $60 billion across private equity, venture capital, credit, special opportunities, and related investment strategies.
The company operates as a subsidiary of Abu Dhabi-based Mubadala Investment Company, combining institutional capital resources with a global alternative asset management platform.
Mubadala Capital maintains offices in Abu Dhabi, London, New York, Rio de Janeiro, and Menlo Park, with more than 250 professionals.
The investment in LSV represents part of its strategy to develop long-term relationships with specialized alternative investment managers.
Through these partnerships, Mubadala Capital aims to provide access to institutional capital, private wealth distribution relationships, and its international network.

articles.title: Blackstone Digital Infrastructure Trust Announces $5 Billion AWS Data Center Transaction
articles.snippet:
Blackstone Digital Infrastructure Trust has agreed to acquire a 75% majority interest in two joint ventures with Amazon Web Services in a transaction valued at approximately $5 billion.
The post Blackstone Digital Infrastructure Trust Announces $5 Billion AWS Data Center Transaction appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Blackstone Digital Infrastructure Trust Announces $5 Billion AWS Data Center Transaction
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 1:04 PM
Blackstone Digital Infrastructure Trust Announces $5 Billion AWS Data Center Transaction
Blackstone Digital Infrastructure Trust has agreed to acquire a 75% majority interest in two joint ventures with Amazon Web Services in a transaction valued at approximately $5 billion.
The acquisition represents the recently listed company’s first investment and carries an initial capitalization rate of 7%. The joint ventures will own 13 newly constructed powered shells across two AWS data center campuses.
AWS will retain a 25% interest in the ventures and lease the entire portfolio on a triple-net basis. The initial lease term is 12 years, with extensions potentially taking the total term to 32 years.
The transaction is expected to close in the fourth quarter of 2026, subject to closing conditions.
The investment establishes a starting portfolio aligned with the trust’s strategy of acquiring stabilized data centers leased to major cloud providers under long-term contracts.
CEO and President Nick Pell identified asset quality, pricing and the tenant relationship as reasons for deploying proceeds from the company’s initial public offering into the portfolio.
For AWS, the arrangement combines continued occupancy with minority ownership. The company said the partnership supports its expansion while maintaining its focus on local employment, workforce training and community priorities.
Blackstone Digital Infrastructure Trust targets newly constructed, income-generating facilities leased to investment-grade hyperscale tenants. Its strategy emphasizes contractual cash flows, rent increases and further acquisitions.
The company is externally managed by a Blackstone affiliate. Blackstone manages nearly $1.4 trillion across real estate, private equity, credit, infrastructure and other strategies.
Morgan Stanley, CBRE Capital Markets, Citi, Goldman Sachs, J.P. Morgan and Wells Fargo are serving as financial advisors on the transaction. Simpson Thacher & Bartlett is advising Blackstone legally.
KEY QUOTES
“We are thrilled to announce BXDC’s inaugural investment and our partnership with Amazon, a leading global technology company with a long-term commitment to innovation. The quality, basis and tenant profile of these assets make this an attractive match for the deployment of our IPO proceeds. Given the deep expertise across our platform, we believe BXDC is well positioned to capitalize on a highly compelling opportunity and deliver value for our shareholders.”
Nick Pell, CEO And President Of Blackstone Digital Infrastructure Trust
“As we scale to meet growing demand for our customers, we’re committed to building in a way that strengthens the communities where we operate. We’re focused on delivering long-term local benefits, from creating good jobs and free workforce training programs to supporting local priorities. Partnering with Blackstone allows us to continue expanding responsibly while keeping communities at the center of how we build.”
Prasad Kalyanaraman, Vice President Of AWS Infrastructure
